title: Hedge Funds Go Underweight AI for First Time Since Early 2023 After $5T Rout
summary:
Hedge funds have moved underweight the broader AI trade for the first time since early 2023, according to Morgan Stanley prime brokerage data, as combined summer and October position cuts created what the bank called "the largest sustained stretch of L/S fund de-risking in over 15 years, as gross exposure never fully recovered between episodes." Cumulative gross flow is down 8% from its June peak, though short covering accounted for the bulk of the week's buying, lifting US long/short net leverage by 5 percentage points to 51% while gross leverage slipped 1 point to 207%.

Goldman Sachs data shows hedge funds sold AI stocks for five straight sessions from Oct. 8 to Oct. 14, wiping out all of their AI buying since the start of 2025, and liquidated long positions roughly 3.5 times faster than they added new shorts. From Oct. 6 through Oct. 30, 47 AI and semiconductor stocks lost about $5 trillion in market value while 625 other large US stocks gained $1.3 trillion, and Morgan Stanley's AI stock basket fell 18% in October against a 2% gain for the average US stock.

The rotation out of capital-intensive AI builders has left Apple as the only Magnificent Seven stock outperforming the S&P 500 this year, up 28% year to date after largely avoiding the AI capital spending binge draining free cash flow at its hyperscaler peers. Apple closed Friday at a $5.03 trillion market capitalization to overtake Nvidia at $4.94 trillion as the world's most valuable company, reversing a $903 billion lead Nvidia held on Oct. 6.

🚨 The AI BUBBLE is starting to look like a MUCH bigger problem than overpriced tech stocks

More than $2 TRILLION was on track to be wiped off the Nasdaq 100 in October, and now Wall Street is getting nervous about something far more dangerous: DEBT.

Blackstone expects Anthropic to receive a JUNK credit rating after its IPO, according to the FT, even as the company plans more than $800 BILLION in computing investments through 2045.

Amazon is burning through cash. Alphabet just lost roughly $500 billion in market value in ONE DAY. And CoreWeave's borrowing costs have reached levels that would make most companies sweat.

Here's where things get crazy.

AI companies are borrowing BILLIONS to buy chips from suppliers who are increasingly helping finance the very customers buying those chips.

That's a LOT of money moving around the same circle.

And the entire industry is just betting that future AI revenues will eventually justify the enormous costs of building all this infrastructure.

Nobody is even questioning whether AI is actually useful.

They're rather questioning whether the spent TRILLIONS to build it will ever make returns.

And if the debt markets lose confidence before those profits arrive, this could get ugly VERY quickly.

Writer: Oliver
selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
Wall Street is obliterating BIG TECH, with Intel plunging nearly 30% and AMD losing more than 11%.

And the rest of the market? Surprisingly calm.

Nvidia is down 4.32%, Broadcom 5.63%, while Microsoft and Amazon are also in the red.

But ENERGY, UTILITIES, REAL ESTATE and parts of healthcare are actually gaining.

Money isn't fleeing the entire stock market. The selling is concentrated in technology, with chipmakers taking the worst hits.

That's what makes this selloff so interesting.

The companies that helped drive Wall Street's AI boom are now taking some of its biggest losses, while investors find opportunities elsewhere.

Writer: Oliver
